translationRepairs: At Dunqiu a great downpour struck, and the emperor wanted to withdraw. Yanshou urged him, saying, "The Jin forces are camped on the river and dare not come out; if we press straight into Chunzhou and seize their bridge, Jin will not be hard to subdue."

At Dunqiu a great downpour struck, and the emperor wanted to withdraw. Yanshou urged him, saying, "The Jin forces are camped on the river and dare not come out; if we press straight into Chanzhou and seize their bridge, Jin will not be hard to subdue."
Focus unit has 若徑入澶州; 澶州 romanizes as Chanzhou (also Danzhou), whereas Chunzhou would be 春州. The proposed replacement corrects only that place-name and leaves the rest of the speech intact.
By then the Jin army had already fallen back to Chunzhou; when Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, Yanshou led light troops out to give battle;
By then the Jin army had already fallen back to Chanzhou; when Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, Yanshou led light troops out to give battle;
Focus unit has 適晉軍先歸澶州; the same 澶州→Chunzhou error as in s0049. Chanzhou matches the Chinese place-name and the rest of the sentence is otherwise faithful.

At Dunqiu they encountered heavy rains; the emperor wished to withdraw the army. Yanshou remonstrated, saying, "The Jin army is encamped on the riverbank and dares not come out to fight; if we go straight into Chunzhou and seize its bridge, then Jin will not be hard to pacify."

At Dunqiu they encountered heavy rains; the emperor wished to withdraw the army. Yanshou remonstrated, saying, "The Jin army is encamped on the riverbank and dares not come out to fight; if we go straight into Chanzhou and seize its bridge, then Jin will not be hard to pacify."
The literal likewise turns 澶州 into Chunzhou in Yanshou’s remonstrance; Chanzhou is the accurate English for 澶州 and leaves the surrounding wording unchanged.
Just then the Jin army had already returned to Chunzhou; Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, and Yanshou led light troops to meet them in battle;
Just then the Jin army had already returned to Chanzhou; Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, and Yanshou led light troops to meet them in battle;
Literal 先歸澶州 must read Chanzhou, not Chunzhou; the proposed fix corrects only that mistranslation.
Early in the Qingtai era he was made Duke of Lu, again became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and took charge at Xuzhou.
Early in the Qingtai era he was made Duke of Lu, again became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and took charge at Xu Prefecture.

Focus unit has 鎮許州; 許州 is Xu Prefecture (around Xuchang), not 徐州. Bare “Xuzhou” invents the wrong place, but the proposed “Xu prefecture (Xuzhou)” is awkward and reintroduces the 徐州 reading; “Xu Prefecture” is the accurate, natural correction.
His father Kuai had been magistrate of Shuo.
His father Kuai had been magistrate of Tiao.
Focus unit has 令蓚; 蓚 (also 蓨) is Tiao county, whereas Shuo would be 朔. The proposed Tiao restores the place-name; the father’s name and office wording are otherwise unchanged.
His father Kuai was magistrate of Shuo.
His father Kuai was magistrate of Tiao.
The literal likewise renders 蓚 as Shuo; Tiao matches the Chinese place-name and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
